A simplified view of the workflow.

The problem

Knowing that AI is useful is different from knowing how to use it in the work a team already does. The gap includes process clarity, confidence, and ownership.

The approach

I created the AI Capability Ladder: AI fluency, workflow mapping, SOP improvement, AI-assisted building, and handoff. Clarity Works delivers this through a 30-day Sprint and a longer Partner Program.

I run discovery with business owners, translate the operational pain into a practical plan, and build function-specific prompt libraries, guides, exercises, and SOPs. The aim is to leave the team able to keep going.

The builder’s perspective

Building systems myself helps me teach from application. It also gives the engagement a practical constraint: the workflow must be understandable and usable by the people who will own it.

The next proof point

The method and learning assets are established parts of the practice. A fuller case study will benefit from client-approved examples and measured adoption over time.
